details.errorCorrection: Choosing arbitrary jobs changes the contract, and loading all rows preserves the expensive scan and sort.
details.boundaryOrTradeoff: A full history endpoint may still need all jobs; this dashboard asks for a bounded pending view.
details.transfer: Push a measured filter, ordering, and limit to the data access boundary when the consumer needs only that subset.

messages.text: Sorting every job in the application still loads the completed rows and does not push the measured pending filter or oldest-first order into the query.
Any twenty pending jobs can omit older pending jobs; the dashboard specifically needs the oldest twenty.
An indefinite cache of the whole table can show completed or newly changed jobs as though they were current pending work.
Loading every job increases the returned set but still does the filter and sort work that the profile measured; the view needs only twenty pending rows.

feedback.reason: The result needs the oldest pending subset, not a full ordering of completed jobs. Filtering and limiting at the query boundary matches the measured access pattern. The query returns the first 20 pending jobs in creation-time order.

options.text: Filter to pending jobs and order by creation time before returning 20.
Sort all jobs in the application and discard completed jobs after loading them.
Return any 20 pending jobs and let the dashboard infer which are oldest.
Cache the complete job table indefinitely, including completed jobs.
Increase the page size so one request loads every job.

prompt: A queue dashboard shows the oldest pending jobs. Which measured query change is appropriate?
